labels.og_answer: The largest adults just under 14 m (46 ft), by a model

top.answer: The largest adults of Spinosaurus aegyptiacus were just under 14 m (46 ft) long and about 7.4 tonnes, by a model of 2022. Nobody has found a whole skeleton. Ours is a young one of about 10 m (33 ft), about three quarters of full size and about 3 to 4 tonnes by a model. Beside the person of 1.70 m, its hip joint sits at about head height, and it is almost six people long.
top.answer_more: Compared with T. rex, the largest Spinosaurus was longer, most likely lighter and much lower at the hips. The two never met: about 30 million years and two continents lay between them.

scale.what: Our Spinosaurus beside a person 1.70 m tall, to one scale: a young one of about 10 m (33 ft), built on the skeleton from Morocco. The pale outline behind it is the largest adults' size by the model of 2022, just under 14 m (46 ft): our model enlarged by about a third. The outline is an estimate, not an animal anyone found. In the pose of our model, the outline measures about 13.2 m end to end.

close.what: The head and the front of the body, closer up, with the person. The snout is long and narrow, the teeth are cones without a saw edge, the nostrils sit far back. The low crest in front of the eyes is certain, its height is not: its top edge is broken on every piece found. The lips are a choice, not a find.
close.alt: The head and front of the Spinosaurus, closer up, the long narrow snout with cone-shaped teeth, a low crest in front of the eye, beside the grey person.

guess.q: How old was the young animal from Morocco when it died?
guess.a: About 17 years, by the growth rings in its thigh bone, give or take two years. It was not full grown.

out.text: The wing for this animal is still being built. The Leonardo da Vinci wing is open today.

blocks.nav: Spinosaurus vs T. rex, size only
blocks.h: Spinosaurus vs T. rex, size only
paras: The largest Spinosaurus was longer than any T. rex found so far: just under 14 m (46 ft) by a model, against about 12 m (39 ft) for SUE's skeleton. It was most likely not heavier: about 7.4 to 8 tonnes in the model, against about 8 to 9 tonnes for the largest known T. rex. At the hips it stood much lower. The thigh bone of the young animal from Morocco is 61 cm, SUE's is 1.32 m. The two never met: Spinosaurus lived about 95 million years ago in North Africa, T. rex about 68 to 66 million years ago in North America.

scale.what: Our Spinosaurus and our T. rex, to one scale. Our Spinosaurus is a young one of about 10 m (33 ft), our T. rex after SUE a large adult of about 11.4 m (37 ft), so the T. rex is the longer one here. An adult Spinosaurus was longer than any T. rex found so far, most likely lighter and much lower at the hips.
scale.alt: A Spinosaurus with a sail on its back and a slightly longer T. rex with its head raised, both from the side, the T. rex about twice as high at the hips, beside the grey person.

Our T. rex, after SUE, about 11.4 m

paras: It stood and walked on two legs, its weight over the hind feet. The four-legged animal of 2014 rested on a calculation error, reported in 2024.

The tail was deep and flat from side to side, like a blade: tall spines above, long bones below. We know that from the Moroccan animal's own tail bones. What it was for is argued: swimming or display.

The spines are known, the tallest on Stromer's skeleton about 1.65 m (5.4 ft) of bone. The shape of the sail above them nobody knows. A thin skin over the spines is the most likely reading, and display is the leading idea of what the sail was for.
The snout widened at the tip like a spoon. No spinosaur has left us its skin, lips or colour.

It lived by the water and ate fish, as its teeth and the isotopes in them suggest. Whether it swam after the fish, or waded and waited for them in the shallows, is argued. The case for swimming rests on the deep tail of 2020 and on dense bones in a study of 2022. Most work since 2021 points to wading. Models find it too buoyant to dive, its skull shape fits an ambush hunter, and the bone-density method was called unreliable in 2024. The museums keep the question open, and so do we.

In the autumn of 1912 the first bones came to light in the Bahariya Oasis in Egypt. They were the lower jaw's front half, 72 cm long, and back, hip and tail bones with the tall spines of the sail. Stromer described them in 1915 and named the animal Spinosaurus after those spines. The skeleton was shown in Munich and was destroyed in a bombing raid in 1944. Only Stromer's notes, drawings and a few photographs survive. Munich holds a Spinosaurus tooth today, not a skeleton.

In 2008 a collector found the first bones near Zrigat in south-eastern Morocco, in the Kem Kem beds. The site was dug out in 2013, the tail from 2015 to 2019. Since 2014 this skeleton has been the species' new type, because Stromer's bones are gone. It is kept in Casablanca.

points: The hips on both sides, both legs, an ankle bone and a nearly complete foot.
The tail, more than 30 bones, about four fifths of its length.
Parts of neck, back and hip bones, pieces of rib, pieces of the skull and one finger bone.
The spines of the sail and the lower jaw: after Stromer's lost skeleton.
The snout: after the adult snout in Milan, scaled down.
The back of the skull, the arms and the hands: after relatives.
The neck, most of the back, the ribs, the shoulder and the end of the tail: other finds, or restored.

end: So every reconstruction is one animal made of several, ours too.

scale.alt: Our Spinosaurus as a skeleton: hips, legs and tail dark red, the sail's spines and the lower jaw blue, skull, neck, ribs and arms pale, beside the person.

key.text: Dark red: the young Moroccan animal's own bones, the hips, both legs, the foot and the tail to its 41st bone, more than 30 of those bones found, the gaps coloured with them.
Blue: after Stromer's lost skeleton from Egypt, the spines of the sail and the lower jaw, its rear half restored.
Pale: after other finds or restored, the snout, the back of the skull, the neck, the ribs, the shoulder, the arms and the end of the tail.

key: Three parts mix two sources and carry the borrowed colour: the skull, the sacrum and the back bones with the tall spines. The small pieces of its own neck, ribs and hand are not coloured apart.

paras: Three things decide every number on this page.

points: Every adult length is a model:
nobody has an adult skeleton. The researchers enlarged the young skeleton from Morocco by about a third, to fit the largest snout found. The snout is real, the body around it is a calculation.
The weight comes from a body model:
build flesh around the skeleton, measure the volume, multiply by a density. For Spinosaurus the air spaces in the neck and body alone move the answer by about 600 kg.
our animal is a young one, and its numbers are its own. So three numbers stand apart here: our animal, the largest adults by the model, and Stromer's skeleton.

blocks.intro: For each number: where it came from, and what it means.

rows.text: The top of a 2005 range of 16 to 18 m: a whole body drawn around the big snout in Milan, with the build of a long-legged relative. We have not read the study's exact range ourselves. Spinosaurus turned out to have short legs, so that body came out too long. The model of 2022 gives just under 14 m, though some museum texts still give 18 m.
The digital skeleton of 2014, scaled up to adult size. The same team's better model of 2022 came out more than a metre shorter.

A calculation of 2007 from the skull's length, with a formula built on other meat-eating dinosaurs: a shorter, much heavier animal. We have not read the study's exact range ourselves. The body model of 2022 gives the largest adults 7.4 to 8 tonnes.
The current model's figure for the largest adults, about 7.4 tonnes. It does not apply to our young one, about 3 to 4 tonnes.
No. Spinosaurus is the longest meat-eating dinosaur known. In the sea, megalodon was longer, at about 16 m (52 ft). T. rex was most likely heavier, and it certainly stood higher at the hips.
From the study of 2014. Its calculation of where the body's weight sat added the air inside the body instead of taking it away. One of its own authors reported that in 2024.
A headline of 2020 about the newly found tail. The study itself calls the tail an organ of propulsion, and whether the animal swam after its fish is argued, not settled.

paras: It is built to the measurements of the young Moroccan animal's own bones, the rest after Stromer's skeleton, other finds and relatives. The arc of the sail and the colours are ours, because neither is known.

items.a: Our young one: the top of the sail about 3.5 m (11.5 ft), the head about 3 m (10 ft) in its pose. Its hip joint sits about 1.6 m (5.2 ft) up. For adults no hip height is published, only that T. rex stood higher at the hips.
No. The long-necked dinosaurs were far bigger: Argentinosaurus about 30 to 35 m (98 to 115 ft) long and roughly 65 to 80 tonnes. More on the biggest dinosaurs page.
